newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cockerill sees rise in steel demand.
newsitem.headline: Cockerill sees rise in steel demand.

text.p: Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre said on Thursday it expected both steel volumes and demand to increase in the second half of 1996, as a result of de-stocking among customers and at distribution centres.
"Stocks are being exhausted and we are feeding real consumption," Cockerill Chairman Jean Gandois told a news conference.

Cockerill said orders for the fourth quarter had seen the end of a fall in prices for all products, and some prices were showing the first signs of rising. It said less pressure from imports coming into the European Union should sustain the trend.
Cockerill said that during the first half of 1996 the steel-making situation worsened in Western Europe, especially in the company's major markets -- Germany, France and Benelux.
Cockerill said it had to reduce prices considerably compared with 1995.

Also weighing on results were first half losses at both its engineering subsidiary Cockerill Mechanical Industries (CMI) and at German unit Ymos YMOSG.F. CMI made a net loss of 368 million francs, although orders placed during the first six months of 1996 showed strong growth. It aims to return to breakeven in 1998 as the result of a relaunch plan.
Cockerill said the group share of the net loss sustained by Ymos was 502 million francs.
"New strategic decisions should soon redirect the future activities of this subsidiary," it said in a statement. Gandois declined to give further details on the decisions that would be taken.
